name: Gaddi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Checked Bailey 1908 'Languages of the Northern Himalayas' (archive.org, full text): Gadi grammar section has no word-stress statement; no other stress source found.

sources.citation: Kumari, Preeti; Mehta, Shreya; Nair, Anjali; Nayak, Anusuya; Roy, Yangchen; Sharma, Vyom. 2026. A Grammar of Gaddi (Grammars of World and Minority Languages). London: UCL Press. xvi+133 pp. doi:10.14324/111.9781800089938 (open access via OAPEN handle 20.500.12657/111079).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. 2 'Phonetics and phonology' (pp. 11-38) has sections on vowels, consonants, phonotactics, clusters, syllable structure, syllable division, nasalisation, prenasalisation, gemination, schwa epenthesis, glide formation, retroflexion, morphophonology -- but NO section on stress, accent, tone or suprasegmentals. Only incidental mentions: p.17 'There is a short unstressed vowel schwa /ə/ that is present after every word-final consonant'; p.36 speculation that sonorant gemination before ergative -ɛ (sjəmm.ɛ, bisɑll.ɛ, ɾidʒʋɑnn.ɛ) 'could be.. a result of stressed syllables with monomoraic lax vow…

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1916. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX Part IV: Specimens of the Pahari languages. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. 'Gadi or Bharmauri' pp. 792ff (Chameali group).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Pronunciation' paragraph treats vowel changes (a>u, a>i), ś > kh [x], r-insertion, de-aspiration; declension/conjugation follow. No accent/stress remark in the Gadi section (the 'change of accent' remark at djvu 102550 belongs to the Chameali static participle discussion).

sources.citation: Dar, Hilal Ahmad. 2022. Phonological and Morphological Analysis of Gaddi Language: A Descriptive Study. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, University of Kashmir, Srinagar (supervisor Aejaz Mohammed Sheikh). Shodhganga hdl 10603/426314.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. 3 'Phonology' (pp. 24-51): inventory (33 C, 16 V + 7 diphthongs), contrasts, distribution, clusters, gemination, syllable structure and patterns (3.19-3.20). The chapter intro says 'the suprasegmental features include the syllable patterns, stress patterns, etc.' but no stress section follows; syllable patterns are the only suprasegmental topic treated. Silent on stress placement. Describes the Gaddi of Bhaderwah/Doda (J&K migrant community from Chamba).

sources.citation: Mehta, Shreya. 2021. The Morphological Realization of Tense, Aspect and Mood in Gaddi, Kinnauri, Kullui and Spiti. PhD thesis, Centre for Linguistics, Jawaharlal Nehru University. Shodhganga hdl 10603/461096.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Section 2.1.2 'The Sound System of Gaddi' (pp. 33-35) gives vowel and consonant charts (8 oral vowels, nasal vowels, four-way stop contrast) only; nothing on stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: Gopalakrishnan, N. 'Bharmauri/Gaddi', ch. 2 in: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India. Linguistic Survey of India: Himachal Pradesh (LSI-HP, post-2011 census volume; archive.org item PARI.linguistic-survey-of-india---himachal-pradesh, dated 2023).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 2.1.2 'Suprasegmental phonemes' (printed p.64) says only: 'In Bharmauri/Gaddi Length and Nasalization realized with long vowels. Some Supra-Segmental vowel phonemes are also found in this mother tongue' followed by a vowel chart and nasalization examples. Section 2.5 'Syllable' (p.~85) has generic boilerplate ('Syllables.. can influence the rhythm of a language, its prosody, its poetic meter and its stress patterns') and CV-pattern lists. No stress-placement statement anywhere in the chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent the chapter for stress/accent/tone/pitch returns only th…

sources.citation: Bailey, T. Grahame. 1908. The Languages of the Northern Himalayas, being studies in the grammar of twenty-six Himalayan dialects. London: Royal Asiatic Society. Part 'Kangri and Gadi': Introduction, 'Grammar of Gadi' pp. 19-41, and O'Brien & Bailey 'Notes on the Gadi dialect of the Kangra Gaddis'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bailey's Gadi introduction notes only the kh-for-s pronunciation; O'Brien's notes are declension/conjugation paradigms and songs. No accent or stress statement for Gadi (the volume's scattered '(accent on second/last syllable)' glosses belong to other dialects' word lists). Confirms the earlier scan's finding.
